Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Saral Singh,Ujjwal Shukla
Hon'ble Krishan Pahal,J.
1.
List has been revised.
Rejoinder affidavit filed by learned counsel for the applicant is taken on record.

2. Heard Sri Arvind Kumar Srivastava, learned Advocate holding brief for Sri Mukesh Kumar,
learned counsel for applicant as well as Sri V.K.S. Parmar, learned A.G.A. for State and also perused the material available on record.
Learned counsel for the informant is not present.

3. The present application for anticipatory bail has been filed for protection in regard to FIR/Case Crime No. 63 of 2022, under Sections 419, 420, 406, 467, 468, 504, 506, 120-B I.P.C., P.S.- Jhunsi,
Rachna Saxena vs State Of U.P. And

1 District- Prayagraj.
4.
Learned counsel for the applicant has stated that the applicant is maliciously being prosecuted in the present case due to ulterior motive and has the apprehension of her arrest.
The applicant has nothing to do with the said offence as alleged by the prosecution.
She is not named in the FIR.
She has simply been made an accused on the basis that she happens to be the wife of the main accused person Mukesh Saxena.
The main allegations are against him.

The criminal history of three more cases assigned to the applicant has been explained in paragraph 4 of the rejoinder affidavit, as she has been enlarged on anticipatory bail by the trial court in all of them.
5. Several other submissions have been made on behalf of the applicant to demonstrate the falsity of the allegations made against her.
The circumstances which, as per counsel, led to the false implication of the applicant have also been touched upon at length.
In case, the anticipatory bail application of the applicant is allowed, she will not misuse the liberty and shall cooperate with trial.

6. On the other hand, learned A.G.A. has vehemently opposed the prayer for grant of anticipatory bail on the ground that final report (charge sheet) has been submitted against the co-accused persons and the applicant is absconding and is not traceable at the address given at Jhunsi, as such,
she is not co-operating with the investigation and there is every likelihood that she shall not co-operate in future also.
Learned A.G.A. has also stated that the applicant is having criminal history of three more cases of similar nature, therefore, she is not entitled for anticipatory bail.

7. Considering the rival submissions advanced by the learned counsel for the parties and also the fact that the applicant is not co-operating with the investigation, coupled with the fact that she has criminal history of three more cases, I do not find it a fit case for grant of anticipatory bail to the applicant as the arguments advanced by learned counsel for the applicant pertain to regular bail application and cannot be agitated at this stage u/s 438 Cr.P.C.
8.

In view of the above, the present anticipatory bail application is found devoid of merits and is,
accordingly, rejected.

9. It is clarified that the observations made herein are limited to the facts brought in by the parties pertaining to the disposal of anticipatory bail application and the said observations shall have no bearing on the merits of the case.

(Justice Krishan Pahal) Order Date :- 16.12.2023 Shalini  Rachna Saxena vs State Of U.P. And Another on 16 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/195972670/
